name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_STATEMENTBASED4_Q01 - Preparation and properties of dinitrogen, ammonia, and nitric acid

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding nitrogen and its compounds:

Statement I: Very pure dinitrogen gas can be obtained by the thermal decomposition of sodium azide or barium azide.

Statement II: In Haber's process for the manufacture of ammonia, high pressure and a catalyst such as iron oxide with small amounts of \(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) are used.

Statement III: Ammonia acts as a Lewis base because the nitrogen atom has one lone pair of electrons available for donation.

Statement IV: Concentrated nitric acid dissolves aluminium and chromium readily by forming soluble nitrates without any surface passivation.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The chemistry of dinitrogen, ammonia, and nitric acid involves thermal decomposition of azides, catalytic equilibrium in ammonia synthesis, Lewis basicity due to lone-pair availability, and oxidative passivation of certain metals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pure Dinitrogen Preparation
Thermal decomposition of sodium azide (\(\mathrm{NaN}_3\)) or barium azide (\(\mathrm{Ba(N_3)_2}\)) yields very pure dinitrogen gas along with the corresponding metal:
\[2\mathrm{NaN}_3 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Na} + 3\mathrm{N}_2\]
\[\mathrm{Ba(N_3)_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ba} + 3\mathrm{N}_2\]
Thus, the claim regarding the preparation of very pure dinitrogen from azides is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Haber's Process Conditions
In the industrial manufacture of ammonia by Haber's process (\(\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})\)), high pressure (about \(200\ \mathrm{atm}\)) favours the forward reaction according to Le Chatelier's principle, and a catalyst of iron oxide with small amounts of \(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{O}\) and \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) is used at \(\sim 700\ \mathrm{K}\) to increase the rate of attainment of equilibrium. Thus, the claim regarding Haber's process is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Lewis Basicity of Ammonia
The nitrogen atom in \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) has three bond pairs and one lone pair of electrons. Because this lone pair is available for donation to electron-deficient species or metal ions, ammonia behaves as a Lewis base. Thus, the claim regarding the Lewis basicity of ammonia is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Reaction of \(\mathrm{Al}\) and \(\mathrm{Cr}\) with Concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\)
Although concentrated nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent that attacks most metals, metals such as chromium (\(\mathrm{Cr}\)) and aluminium (\(\mathrm{Al}\)) do not dissolve in concentrated nitric acid because a thin, protective passive film of oxide forms on their surface. Thus, the claim that aluminium and chromium dissolve readily without passivation is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding pure dinitrogen preparation from azides, Haber's process conditions, and the Lewis basicity of ammonia are correct, whereas the claim regarding the dissolution of aluminium and chromium in concentrated nitric acid is incorrect.

answer.text: Only II, III, and IV are correct
Only I, II, and III are correct
All I, II, III, and IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_STATEMENTBASED4_Q02 - Allotropes of phosphorus, phosphine, and phosphorus halides

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding phosphorus and its compounds:

Statement I: White phosphorus is more reactive than red phosphorus because of angular strain in the discrete tetrahedral \(\mathrm{P}_4\) molecule where the \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}\) bond angles are \(60^\circ\).

Statement II: Phosphine (\(\mathrm{PH}_3\)) is prepared in the laboratory by heating white phosphorus with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution in an inert atmosphere of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\).

Statement III: In gaseous and liquid phases, \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) has a trigonal bipyramidal structure in which the two axial \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Cl}\) bonds are longer than the three equatorial \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Cl}\) bonds.

Statement IV: Phosphorus trichloride (\(\mathrm{PCl}_3\)) hydrolyses in the presence of moisture to form orthophosphoric acid (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\)) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\).

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The reactivity of phosphorus allotropes, preparation of phosphine, molecular geometry of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\), and hydrolysis of phosphorus halides depend on molecular structure, bond strain, and oxidation state conservation during hydrolysis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reactivity of White vs Red Phosphorus
White phosphorus consists of discrete tetrahedral \(\mathrm{P}_4\) molecules in which the \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}\) bond angles are only \(60^\circ\), introducing significant angular strain. Red phosphorus is polymeric, consisting of chains of \(\mathrm{P}_4\) tetrahedra linked together, making it much more stable and less reactive. Thus, the claim regarding the higher reactivity of white phosphorus due to angular strain is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Laboratory Preparation of Phosphine
In the laboratory, phosphine (\(\mathrm{PH}_3\)) is prepared by heating white phosphorus with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution in an inert atmosphere of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\):
\[\mathrm{P}_4 + 3\mathrm{NaOH} + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{PH}_3 + 3\mathrm{NaH}_2\mathrm{PO}_2\]
Thus, the claim regarding the laboratory preparation of phosphine is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Structure and Bond Lengths of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\)
In gaseous and liquid phases, \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) adopts a trigonal bipyramidal geometry. The two axial \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Cl}\) bond pairs experience greater repulsion from the three equatorial bond pairs than the equatorial bond pairs experience among themselves. Consequently, the two axial \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Cl}\) bonds (\(240\ \mathrm{pm}\)) are longer than the three equatorial \(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Cl}\) bonds (\(202\ \mathrm{pm}\)). Thus, the claim regarding the structure and bond lengths of \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Hydrolysis of \(\mathrm{PCl}_3\)
Phosphorus trichloride (\(\mathrm{PCl}_3\), where phosphorus is in the \(+3\) oxidation state) hydrolyses in the presence of moisture to give orthophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_3\), also \(+3\) oxidation state) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\), not orthophosphoric acid (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\)):
\[\mathrm{PCl}_3 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_3 + 3\mathrm{HCl}\]
Thus, the claim that \(\mathrm{PCl}_3\) hydrolyses to form orthophosphoric acid is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding white phosphorus angular strain, laboratory preparation of phosphine, and axial versus equatorial bond lengths in \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) are correct, whereas the claim regarding the hydrolysis product of \(\mathrm{PCl}_3\) is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I, II, and III are correct
Only II, III, and IV are correct
All I, II, III, and IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_STATEMENTBASED4_Q03 - Group 16 trends, ozone stability, sulphur allotropes, and sulphuric acid

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding Group 16 elements and their compounds:

Statement I: Oxygen has a less negative electron gain enthalpy than sulphur because of the compact nature of the oxygen atom causing higher interelectronic repulsions.

Statement II: Thermodynamic instability of ozone (\(\mathrm{O}_3\)) with respect to dioxygen (\(\mathrm{O}_2\)) arises because its decomposition has both a negative enthalpy change (\(\Delta H < 0\)) and a positive entropy change (\(\Delta S > 0\)).

Statement III: Rhombic sulphur (\(\alpha\)-sulphur) is stable above \(369\ \mathrm{K}\), whereas monoclinic sulphur (\(\beta\)-sulphur) is stable below \(369\ \mathrm{K}\).

Statement IV: For sulphuric acid in aqueous solution, the second dissociation constant \(K_{a_2}\) is much smaller than the first dissociation constant \(K_{a_1}\).

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Trends in Group 16 elements and their compounds are governed by atomic size, thermodynamic parameters (\(\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S\)), allotropic phase transition temperatures, and stepwise acid dissociation equilibria.

Step 2: Evaluation of Electron Gain Enthalpy of Oxygen vs Sulphur
Because of the small, compact size of the oxygen atom (\(2p\) subshell), the incoming electron experiences significant interelectronic repulsion compared to the larger \(3p\) subshell of sulphur. Consequently, oxygen has a less negative electron gain enthalpy (\(-141\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)) than sulphur (\(-200\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)). Thus, the claim regarding the electron gain enthalpy of oxygen versus sulphur is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Thermodynamic Instability of Ozone
The decomposition of ozone into dioxygen (\(2\mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 3\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\)) is exothermic (\(\Delta H < 0\)) and accompanied by an increase in the number of gaseous molecules, giving a positive entropy change (\(\Delta S > 0\)). Both effects reinforce each other to produce a large negative Gibbs energy change (\(\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0\)), making ozone thermodynamically unstable with respect to dioxygen. Thus, the claim regarding the thermodynamic instability of ozone is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Thermal Stability of \(\alpha\)- and \(\beta\)-Sulphur
The transition temperature between rhombic sulphur (\(\alpha\)-sulphur) and monoclinic sulphur (\(\beta\)-sulphur) is \(369\ \mathrm{K}\). Rhombic sulphur (\(\alpha\)-sulphur) is the stable form at room temperature and below \(369\ \mathrm{K}\), transforming into monoclinic sulphur (\(\beta\)-sulphur) above \(369\ \mathrm{K}\). Conversely, \(\beta\)-sulphur is stable above \(369\ \mathrm{K}\) and transforms into \(\alpha\)-sulphur below \(369\ \mathrm{K}\). Thus, the claim reversing the stability temperature ranges of \(\alpha\)- and \(\beta\)-sulphur is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of Stepwise Dissociation Constants of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\)
In aqueous solution, sulphuric acid ionises in two steps:
\[\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{HSO}_4^-(\mathrm{aq}); \quad K_{a_1} > 10\]
\[\mathrm{HSO}_4^-(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}(\mathrm{aq}); \quad K_{a_2} = 1.2 \times 10^{-2}\]
Because it is much more difficult to remove a proton from the negatively charged \(\mathrm{HSO}_4^-\) ion than from neutral \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\), \(K_{a_2}\) is much smaller than \(K_{a_1}\). Thus, the claim regarding the dissociation constants of sulphuric acid is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the electron gain enthalpy of oxygen versus sulphur, the thermodynamic instability of ozone, and the relative magnitudes of \(K_{a_1}\) and \(K_{a_2}\) for sulphuric acid are correct, whereas the claim regarding the stability temperature ranges of rhombic and monoclinic sulphur is incorrect.

answer.text: Only I, III, and IV are correct
Only I, II, and IV are correct
